transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well… I’m here because everybody keeps acting like I’m making things up, but I’m not. The hospital people, and some people from the agency too, they’ve been watching our house and even my cleaning routes, like they’re checking up on whether I’m taking proper care of my husband.

And I mean, I know how to clean, I’ve done housekeeping for years, you notice when things are out of place—cars sitting too long, people looking over too much. It’s not just me being nervous. They keep pretending it’s nothing, but I know what I’m seeing.
Do you believe that these people watching you are part of an organized group or agency with a specific purpose, like trying to control or test you in some way?

I don’t know if it’s one big group with a name or anything, but it feels organized, yes. Like the hospital people and some folks from that agency, they keep turning up around our house or around where I clean, and it’s like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband.

And I’ve cleaned in enough places to know when somebody is just sitting there normal and when they’re watching. People think housekeeping is just mops and sheets, but you notice things. So yes, it feels like they’re testing me somehow, even if they won’t say it straight.
Have you ever seen, heard, or sensed things that others around you don’t seem to notice, even when you’re sure they’re real?

Yes… I mean, I have heard things. Not like the TV being on or the neighbors, because I know what that sounds like. Even when the house is quiet, I’ll hear a woman’s voice near the kitchen window, clear as anything, telling me to check the locks or move his pills.

And the kitchen window, it’s old, you know, it rattles when the weather changes, and I’ve told my husband we should get that fixed, but this isn’t the window. It’s a voice, like she’s standing right there. Other people don’t seem to hear it, but I do.
Do you believe, without any doubt, that these people watching you have a specific reason to monitor your actions, such as suspecting you of wrongdoing or wanting to take control of your life?

Yes, I do think there’s a reason. I’m not saying I know every piece of it, but it’s not random. People keep acting like I’m imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some of those agency folks have been watching our house, and even where I go cleaning.

It feels like they’re checking on me, like they think I’m not taking proper care of my husband. And that bothers me because I’ve always kept things in order—at work, at home, you know, when you clean for a living you learn to notice small things. Cars parked where they weren’t before, people looking too long. So yes, I believe they’re watching for that reason.
Do you ever feel like someone is trying to control your thoughts or actions from the outside, or that thoughts are being placed into your mind that aren’t your own?

I don’t know about that exactly. “Placed into my mind” sounds… I mean, I have thoughts all day, everybody does, especially when there’s laundry and pills and dinner and I’m trying to remember if I bought dish soap.

Sometimes I feel pushed, like I should check something or fix something right away, but I don’t know if that’s someone controlling me. I’ve always been particular that way. At the houses I clean, if a towel is folded wrong I can’t just leave it, you know? But thoughts being put in there from outside… I’m not sure. I don’t think I can say that.
Have you ever felt that someone is making you think certain thoughts, or that your thoughts aren’t fully your own, like someone is influencing them from the outside?

I don’t think so… not like someone is putting thoughts in my head. I mean, I get a lot on my mind, and sometimes I’ll be standing there with a mop bucket and suddenly remember three things at once, like the towels, the stove, whether I left the back door unlocked.

But that feels like me, I guess. Or maybe just nerves. It’s hard to tell when you’re tired. I don’t know that I’d say someone outside is making me think things. I haven’t really noticed it that way.
Have you ever felt that everyday events, like something on TV or a conversation you overhear, are directed at you personally, even if others don’t see it that way?

Well… TV, I don’t know, I don’t sit and watch it that closely unless I’m folding clothes or waiting on dinner. But conversations, yes, sometimes it feels like people are saying things in a way they mean for me to hear.

That’s part of why I’m here, really. People keep saying I’m imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some people from that agency have been watching our house, and watching where I go on my cleaning routes. Like they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband. And once you notice that, then little things people say don’t feel accidental anymore, you know? Like they’re hinting at it, but nobody will just come out and say it straight.
Do you ever feel like random events, like something happening on the street or a song playing somewhere, is sending you a message or has a special meaning just for you?

Sometimes, yes… not every little thing, but once you notice people are watching, things start to line up. Like if I’m out on a cleaning job and someone slows down near the house, or says something about “keeping an eye on things,” it feels like it’s meant for me.

I know people keep saying I’m imagining it, but that’s why I’m here. The hospital people, and some people from the agency, they’ve been watching our house and where I go on my cleaning routes. They want to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband. So when something happens out in the street, or somebody makes a comment, it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like part of that.

Do you ever feel that things people do not say directly, like a song on the radio or something happening on the street, are secretly about you or meant for you to notice, even if they don’t seem connected to anything obvious?

Yes… I mean, not like every song is about me or anything. But sometimes things happen and it feels like I’m supposed to notice. Like when someone says something without saying it straight, or they’re near the house at the right time.

That’s why I came in, because people keep acting like I’m imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some folks from that agency have been watching our house. And not just the house—my cleaning routes too. I’ll be carrying supplies or trying to get through a job, and then I notice something, and it’s like… they’re checking up, seeing if I’m taking proper care of my husband. I don’t know why nobody will just say it plainly.

Do you feel like things that happen around you—like something on the news, a car driving by, or even a stranger’s actions—are specifically about you or meant to send you a message, even if others don’t see it that way?

Yes, that’s what I mean… maybe not the news so much, I don’t always follow it, but cars coming by, people around the house, things like that. It feels like it’s about me, like they’re letting me know they’re watching.

I’m here because people keep acting like I’m just imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some folks from that agency have been watching our house. And they know my cleaning routes too, which is… I mean, I’ve been doing that kind of work a long time, you learn who belongs around a place and who doesn’t. They’re checking to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband, but nobody will just say it straight.

I don’t know if they can hear my exact thoughts, like word-for-word… but it feels like they know things they shouldn’t. That’s part of why I’m here, because everybody keeps saying I’m imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some people from the agency have been watching our house.

And not just the house—my cleaning routes too. I go into different places for work, and you start to notice when someone is keeping tabs. I think they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband, but nobody just comes out and says it.
Do you ever feel like your actions are being controlled or influenced by something or someone outside of yourself, beyond just being watched?

Not controlled exactly… I mean, I still do what I do. I go to work, I clean, I take care of things at home. But influenced, maybe, because when you know people are watching, you move different, you think about every little thing.

That’s why I came here. People keep saying I’m imagining it, but I know the hospital people and some folks from that agency have been watching our house, and they know my cleaning routes too. I’ve done housekeeping long enough to notice when someone is out of place. It feels like they’re checking up on whether I’m taking proper care of my husband, but nobody will just come out and say it.

I don’t think someone is putting thoughts in my head, not like that. It’s more that things happening around me are connected, and people act like I’m making it up.

They’re checking to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband, but nobody will just say it straight.

Yes… like, people might say it’s normal for a car to be parked near the house, or someone being in the same building where I’m cleaning, but I know when it’s not just normal.

I came here because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining things, but I know the hospital people and some people from that agency have been watching our house. And then I’ll see somebody around one of my cleaning routes, just standing there or looking like they’re checking something, and it feels connected. They’re watching to see if I’m taking proper care of my husband.

I’ve done cleaning work a long time, so I notice things other people don’t. Like people think because you’re the cleaner you don’t see what’s going on, but you do. And my husband, he needs me to keep things right, so of course I pay attention. But they won’t just come out and say that’s what they’re doing.
Can you think of a time when something happened that seemed completely normal to everyone else, but you felt deep down it was specifically about you, even if they didn't realize it?

I mean, yes… but it’s hard to explain because other people say, “Oh, that’s just somebody parked there,” or “That person just works in the building.” But deep down I know it’s about me.

And not just the house — my cleaning routes too. I’ve worked housekeeping long enough to know when someone is just passing through and when they’re paying attention.

They’re checking if I’m taking proper care of my husband. They won’t say it straight, but that’s what it is. And then everybody wants me to pretend it’s nothing.
Can you think of a time when someone else’s actions, which seemed normal to everyone else, felt to you like they were secretly sending you a message or had a hidden meaning for you specifically?

Well… yes, I guess that’s what I mean. Like when somebody from the hospital or that agency is around, they don’t have to say anything. They can just be standing there, acting like they’re doing paperwork or looking at a phone, but I know what it’s about.

People tell me I’m imagining it, and I know I’ve said that already, but that’s why I came in. They’ve been watching our house, and then I see them around my cleaning routes too. It’s not random. It’s like they’re letting me know they’re checking up on me, seeing if I’m taking proper care of my husband.

And I’ve cleaned places for years, so I notice little things. People think you don’t, but you do. They don’t come right out and say it, but the message is there.
Can you think of a time when others saw or experienced the same thing you did, but interpreted it completely differently, while you still felt your interpretation was the true one?

Yes… like my sister, she’ll say, “That’s just a car parked there,” or “They’re probably doing their job,” and I know how it sounds, I do. But she doesn’t clean buildings like I do. When you’re in people’s homes and offices, you learn to notice when someone is just passing by and when they’re watching.

And then I’ll see the same kind of thing around my cleaning routes, too. Other people see it and say it’s nothing, but to me it’s clear they’re checking whether I’m taking proper care of my husband.

And I mean, I do take care of him. I keep things clean, I make sure things are right. People don’t understand how much work that is. But they look at the same thing I’m looking at and pretend it’s normal, and I just don’t think it is.
